clue.text: The 6dn one developed in old age?

definitions.note: an adjectival phrase: belonging to an ancient period

indicators.note: something developed has been worked up into a new shape, so these letters are rearranged

parts.note: taken as written
the answer to 6 Down, the fellow's name
one is the Roman numeral I

explanation.surface: Someone, perhaps the man named at 6 Down, matured late in life.
explanation.walkthrough: 'developed' rearranges THE, COLIN (from 6 Down) and I. The definition is cheeky, hence the question mark: this is the New Stone Age, though still very old.
explanation.definitionFit: The term describes the later Stone Age, a prehistoric period when farming began, so it belongs to an old era.

clue.text: Material for buttons from northern part of Brazil

parts.note: Acre is a state in the north-west of Brazil

explanation.surface: Button stock sourced from the north of Brazil.
explanation.walkthrough: 'part of Brazil' looks like a hidden-word signal but is the state of Acre.
explanation.definitionFit: Mother-of-pearl, the shiny shell lining, is traditionally cut into buttons.

clue.text: German smuggled inside Italian port

indicators.note: inside means one piece is placed within the other

parts.note: Otto is a typical German man's name
to run goods is to smuggle them, so smuggled is ran

explanation.surface: A German was sneaked into a harbour in Italy.
explanation.walkthrough: 'smuggled' looks like part of the picture, but it gives the letters: to run contraband is to smuggle it.
explanation.definitionFit: A town on the heel of Italy, on the strait joining Adriatic and Ionian Seas.

clue.text: Mounts up, like clothes awaiting ironing?

definitions.meaning: mounts up means grows or rises
read as two words: crumpled garments are full of folds

explanation.surface: A pile of crumpled laundry keeps growing.
explanation.walkthrough: Split the second sense as IN CREASES.
explanation.definitionFit: Growing or rising; and, split in two, crumpled with folds.

clue.text: Chinless wonder's approving cry to king

parts.note: hooray is a cheer of approval
Henry is the name of eight English kings

explanation.surface: A dim aristocrat cheers on the monarch.
explanation.walkthrough: British slang for a loud, foolish upper-class young man; 'chinless wonder' is a similar term for an ineffectual toff.
explanation.definitionFit: Both are British slang for a brash but brainless upper-class young man.

clue.text: Firm head of stock salad ingredient

parts.note: Co. is short for company, a firm

indicators.note: head of signals the first letter of the word stock

explanation.surface: A company boss stocks up on salad.
explanation.walkthrough: This is the cos lettuce, known as romaine in America.
explanation.definitionFit: A crisp, long-leaved lettuce used in salads.

clue.text: Desert transport arrived and then left

parts.note: arrived means came

explanation.surface: A traveller's mount turned up and then set off again.
explanation.definitionFit: The dromedary is the classic beast of burden used for crossing sandy wastes.

clue.text: Fellow presenting pound in its modern 'form

indicators.note: in means one piece sits inside the other

parts.note: the British pound has been a coin rather than a note since 1983
L (from Latin libra) is the symbol for a pound

explanation.surface: A man shows off a pound in its new shape.
explanation.walkthrough: 'in' puts L inside COIN. The pound note was replaced by a coin in Britain in the 1980s.
explanation.definitionFit: It is a man's name, and a crossword fellow or chap is any man.

clue.text: Radio presenter taking brandy on island

parts.note: marc is a brandy distilled from grape skins

explanation.surface: A broadcaster tops up with brandy on an island.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Radio presenter' suggests a DJ; it is the Italian pioneer who gave the world radio.
explanation.definitionFit: Guglielmo of that surname developed wireless telegraphy, effectively bringing radio to the world.

clue.text: Portraitist capturing composer and daughter in scholarly way

indicators.note: capturing means the painter's name holds the other pieces inside

parts.note: Sir Peter Lely was a 17th-century court portrait painter
Thomas Arne was an English composer, of Rule, Britannia!

explanation.surface: A portrait painter depicts a composer with his daughter, in a scholarly manner.
explanation.walkthrough: 'capturing' reads as capturing a likeness on canvas, but it is the container signal; Lely was Charles II's court painter.
explanation.definitionFit: Done with deep learning; erudite or academic in manner.

clue.text: Island's copper turned a vehicle round

parts.note: Cu is the chemical symbol for copper

indicators.note: turned means the words a and vehicle are flipped to read the other way

parts.note: a car is a vehicle
a round shape is the letter O

explanation.surface: A policeman on some island spun a car around.
explanation.walkthrough: 'turned' flips A CAR to give RACA. 'Island's' is the definition with 's for 'has'; 'copper' is the metal, not a policeman.
explanation.definitionFit: It is a Dutch Caribbean island off Venezuela, also known for its liqueur.

clue.text: Thus leather initially goes to a number of tanning establishments

parts.note: so means thus

indicators.note: initially signals that only the opening letter of the word leather is used

parts.note: an aria is a number, a song in an opera

explanation.surface: So hides go off to be tanned in a few workshops.
explanation.walkthrough: 'goes to' just joins the pieces; 'number' is a musical piece, not a figure.
explanation.definitionFit: These are sunrooms or salons with sunbeds, places where people go to brown their skin.

clue.text: Electronic selector that's associated with English navy

parts.note: RN is the Royal Navy
i.e. stands for id est, that is

explanation.surface: Some electronic device is linked with the English fleet.
explanation.walkthrough: This is the British machine (Electronic Random Number Indicator Equipment) that picks winning Premium Bond numbers, a UK government savings lottery.
explanation.definitionFit: The acronym names the computer that randomly chooses Premium Bond prize winners.

clue.text: It's instrumental in rounding up Alpine cattle

definitions.text: It's instrumental in rounding up Alpine cattle

parts.words: It's instrumental in rounding up Alpine cattle
parts.note: read 'instrumental' literally: a musical instrument herdsmen blow in the mountains to call cows home

explanation.surface: Something plays a key part in herding cows in the Alps.
explanation.walkthrough: 'instrumental' looks like 'helpful' but means a musical instrument.
explanation.definitionFit: A very long wooden horn used by Swiss herders to call cattle across the valleys.

clue.text: Experts with criminals representing both sides of the case

parts.note: pros are professionals, experts
and means with, joining two things
cons are convicts, criminals

explanation.surface: Professionals and crooks appear on opposing sides in court.
explanation.walkthrough: 'representing' is a link; 'case' looks legal, matching the courtroom picture.
explanation.definitionFit: The arguments for and against a proposal are its advantages and disadvantages.

clue.text: For example, one's initial sense of self-importance

parts.note: e.g. stands for exempli gratia, for example

indicators.note: initial signals that the first letter of the word one's is taken

explanation.surface: A remark on how vanity first takes hold of a person.
explanation.definitionFit: The word means one's self-esteem, often an inflated opinion of oneself.

clue.text: Taken by objectors, it's not included

definitions.meaning: objectors take offence, the idiom being to take umbrage at something
something left out or outside a rule

explanation.surface: Protesters seize on something that has been left out.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Taken' completes the idiom 'take exception'.
explanation.definitionFit: An omission from a general rule; and objectors take offence, the idiom using this word.

clue.text: Peers in stream with this boy or girl

definitions.text: Peers in stream with this boy or girl

parts.words: Peers in stream with this boy or girl
parts.note: peers are classmates and a stream is a group of pupils of similar ability, so this is a pupil

explanation.surface: Lords gaze into a brook alongside a youngster.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Peers' suggests nobles or looking, and 'stream' a brook; in schools a stream is a set of pupils grouped by ability.
explanation.definitionFit: A pupil of either sex, whose equals sit in the same class grouping.

clue.text: Like 'flag of race, going up and down?

definitions.meaning: the flag waved at the finish of a motor race has black and white squares
a career with ups and downs is described this way

explanation.surface: Like a race flag, waving up and down.
explanation.walkthrough: A career of mixed fortunes is called this, the squares standing for good and bad patches.
explanation.definitionFit: Patterned in squares, like the finishing flag; also, of a history with highs and lows.

clue.text: Maugham's novel form of merrymaking

definitions.meaning: a 1930 novel by W. Somerset Maugham
a phrase for festivity and fun, as in life not being all fun and feasting

explanation.surface: A Somerset Maugham book presents a fresh kind of revelry.
explanation.walkthrough: 'novel' reads as 'new' in the surface but is the book. The phrase is old English slang for good times.
explanation.definitionFit: Both Maugham's satirical book and the idiom for festivity, sweet treats and beer standing for fun.

clue.text: Material' for nails a tinker contrived to make

indicators.note: contrived means put together artfully, so these letters are reshaped

explanation.surface: A tinsmith improvises some stuff to make nails.
explanation.walkthrough: 'contrived' rearranges A TINKER; nails are fingernails, not metal ones.
explanation.definitionFit: The fibrous protein that makes up hair, horns and fingernails.

clue.text: Super tonic, in a word, makes us beam

definitions.meaning: the supertonic is the second note of the scale, sung as re in sol-fa, here in its alternative spelling
a beam is a shaft of light

explanation.surface: A fine tonic drink, in short, makes us smile.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Super tonic' looks like praise for a drink; joined into one word it is the supertonic, the second degree of the scale.
explanation.definitionFit: The sol-fa second note has this spelling, and a shaft of light has the same name.

clue.text: Let in again, registered by American university

parts.note: a meter or gauge that registers a value reads it
MIT is the Massachusetts Institute of Technology

explanation.surface: Someone is allowed back after being enrolled at a US college.
explanation.walkthrough: 'registered' looks like enrolled; it is a dial's showing, as in 'the thermometer read 30'.
explanation.definitionFit: To allow someone entry once more is to take them back in.

clue.text: Graphically described harbour spread out here

parts.note: a port is a harbour
rayed means spread out in lines like rays

explanation.surface: An artist depicts the harbour stretching out below.
explanation.walkthrough: 'here' is a link word.
explanation.definitionFit: To depict something vividly in words or pictures is to show it in that way.

clue.text: Not even a preliminary sketch

explanation.surface: Not so much as an outline drawing.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Not even' looks like 'not so much as'; it means bumpy.
explanation.definitionFit: Uneven or coarse in texture; and a draft drawing before the finished work.

clue.text: Not disposed to take forty winks in middle of duty

indicators.note: in means one piece goes inside the other
middle of signals the central letters of the word duty

parts.note: forty winks is a nap

explanation.surface: Someone is reluctant to doze off while on shift.
explanation.walkthrough: 'to take' only joins the pieces; 'forty winks' is the everyday idiom for a short sleep.
explanation.definitionFit: Unfitted or not inclined; inapt or unsuited in disposition.

clue.text: Fish found in ditch, not river

indicators.note: not means the named letter is taken away

parts.note: a trench is a ditch

explanation.surface: A fish turns up in a ditch rather than a river.
explanation.walkthrough: 'not' removes R from TRENCH.
explanation.definitionFit: A freshwater fish of the carp family that lives in still waters.

clue.text: Enter uninvited, scrambling under it

indicators.note: scrambling means these letters are jumbled into a new order

explanation.surface: Someone barges in, crawling beneath something.
explanation.walkthrough: 'scrambling' rearranges UNDER IT; it looks like crawling.
explanation.definitionFit: To come in where one is unwelcome or unasked is to trespass.

clue.text: One could produce 'electricity, to a certain extent

definitions.text: One could produce 'electricity, to a certain extent

indicators.note: to a certain extent means only part of the words produce electricity is used, spanning the gap

explanation.surface: Something can generate power, up to a point.
explanation.walkthrough: 'to a certain extent' marks the letters straddling 'produce electricity'; the electric version of this fish stuns prey.
explanation.definitionFit: The electric species of this snakelike fish generates strong shocks.

clue.text: One may catch several crabs in a row

definitions.text: One may catch several crabs in a row

parts.words: One may catch several crabs in a row
parts.note: to catch a crab is a rowing blunder, and a row is an outing in a boat

explanation.surface: A fisherman might land a string of crabs one after another.
explanation.walkthrough: 'catch a crab' is rowing slang for a stroke where the blade jams in the water; 'in a row' is the trip, not a line.
explanation.definitionFit: A rower, one who pulls a blade, may fumble several strokes this way.

clue.text: Ordinal carried by parson in Thetford

indicators.note: carried by means the letters are held within the words parson in Thetford

explanation.surface: A number is borne by the vicar in the Norfolk town of Thetford.
explanation.walkthrough: 'carried by' marks the letters within 'parson in Thetford'.
explanation.definitionFit: It is an ordinal number, giving position in a series after the eighth.

clue.text: Endure dump found in ultimate resort

definitions.note: noun phrase for an answer used mostly as an adjective; it also names a final line of defence

parts.note: endure means to keep going, to last
to dump something is to ditch it

explanation.surface: Putting up with being dumped as a final option.
explanation.walkthrough: 'found in' is a link.
explanation.definitionFit: A final desperate attempt or the very end of a defensive line is described this way.
